Malvern Hills' population increased by around 4,900 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population passed 79,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Malvern Hills increased by 6.5%, from just over 74,600 in 2011 to around 79,500 in 2021.

The population here increased by a greater percentage than the overall population of the West Midlands (6.2%), but at a similar rate to the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, Malvern Hills was home to around 1.0 person per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 0.9 in 2011. This area was the joint third-least densely populated local authority area across the West Midlands (after Herefordshire and Shropshire).

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was similar in Malvern Hills to the West Midlands as a whole

An older Malvern Hills

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of Malvern Hills increased by three years, from 47 to 50 years of age.

This area had the highest average (median) age in the West Midlands and a higher average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 65 to 74 years rose by around 2,100 (an increase of 23.1%), while the number of residents between 35 and 49 years fell by around 2,100 (14.5% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 65 and 74 years increased by 1.9 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Unpaid care in Malvern Hills

Malvern Hills saw England's third-largest percentage-point fall in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care (from 8.7% in 2011 to 5.1% in 2021). These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

England's largest decreases in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care occurred in Derbyshire Dales (from 9.0% to 5.3%) and Pendle (from 7.9% to 4.2%).

Every local authority area across the West Midlands saw a fall in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care, as the regional proportion fell from 7.4% to 4.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Malvern Hills decreased by 3.6 percentage points

Change in housing in Malvern Hills

Of Malvern Hills households, 71.0% owned their home in 2021, down from 71.9% in 2011.

In 2021, just over one in eight households (13.3%) rented privately, compared with 11.5% in 2011. The percentage of Malvern Hills households that lived in a socially rented property increased from 14.1% to 14.3%.

The decrease in the percentage of households that owned their home was greater across the West Midlands (2.1 percentage points, from 64.9% to 62.8%) than in Malvern Hills (0.9 percentage points). Across England, the percentage fell by 2.0 percentage points, from 63.3% to 61.3%.

The rate of home ownership in Malvern Hills decreased by 0.9 percentage points

Disability in Malvern Hills

In 2021, 6.4% of Malvern Hills residents were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. This figure decreased from 7.4% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just over 1 in 10 people (10.5%) were identified as being disabled and limited a little, compared with 9.6% in 2011. The proportion of Malvern Hills residents who were not disabled increased from 83.0% to 83.1%.

The decrease in the proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot was greater across the West Midlands (1.9 percentage points, from 9.9% to 8.0%) than in Malvern Hills (1.0 percentage points). Across England, the proportion fell by 1.6 percentage points, from 9.1% to 7.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Malvern Hills decreased by 1.0 percentage points

Change in work hours

Malvern Hills saw the West Midlands' third-largest percentage-point rise in the proportion of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week (from 11.5% in 2011 to 12.3% in 2021).

Across the region, only Birmingham (from 10.0% to 11.2%) and Sandwell (from 8.0% to 9.0%) saw a greater increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults who worked 15 hours or less in Malvern Hills increased by 0.8 percentage points

Malvern Hills residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 71,700 Malvern Hills residents said they were born in England. This represented 90.3% of the local population. The figure has risen from just over 67,700 in 2011, which at the time represented 90.8% of Malvern Hills' population.

Wales was the next most represented, with around 1,900 Malvern Hills residents reporting this country of birth (2.4%). This figure has remained relatively unchanged from 2011.

The number of Malvern Hills residents born in Scotland remained close to 900 between the last two census (from 1.2% of the local population in 2011 to 1.1% in 2021)

In 2021, 90.3% of Malvern Hills residents reported their country of birth as England

Religion in Malvern Hills

In 2021, 38.1% of Malvern Hills residents reported having "No religion", up from 23.9% in 2011. The rise of 14.3 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in Malvern Hills. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across the West Midlands, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 22.0% to 32.9%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 53.9% of people in Malvern Hills described themselves as Christian (down from 67.5%), while 6.2% did not state their religion (down from 7.3% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

Family in Malvern Hills

In 2021, 6.6% of Malvern Hills households included a couple with only non-dependent children. This figure increased from 6.1% in 2011.

Malvern Hills saw the West Midlands' joint largest rise (alongside Rugby, Worcester and Wolverhampton) in the percentage of households including a couple with only non-dependent children. This area had the region’s tenth lowest percentage of households including a couple with only non-dependent children.

The percentage of households including a couple with only non-dependent children in Malvern Hills increased by 0.5 percentage points

Health in Malvern Hills

In 2021, 50.3% of Malvern Hills residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 48.4% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 34.6% to 33.8%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Malvern Hills residents describing their health as "very bad" decreased from 1.2% to 0.9%, while those describing their health as "bad" fell from 3.5% to 3.3%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in bad health in Malvern Hills decreased by 0.2 percentage points

National identity in Malvern Hills

In 2021, 3.2% of Malvern Hills residents did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK. This figure increased from 2.6% in 2011.

In 2021, 1.3% of residents identified with a UK and non-UK national identity, compared with 0.5% in 2011. The percentage of residents in Malvern Hills that identified as "British only" increased from 16.4% to 56.8%.

The increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK was greater across the West Midlands (2.5 percentage points, from 6.2% to 8.7%) than in Malvern Hills (0.6 percentage points). Across England, the percentage increased by 1.7 percentage points, from 8.2% to 10.0%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in Malvern Hills increased by 0.6 percentage points

More adults never married or in a civil partnership

Of Malvern Hills residents aged 16 years and over, 28.6% said they had never been married or in a civil partnership in 2021, up from 26.2% in 2011.

In 2021, just over one in two people (51.8%) said they were married or in a registered civil partnership, compared with 53.8% in 2011. The percentage of adults in Malvern Hills that had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership increased from 9.4% to 9.8%.

This area had the region’s second lowest percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership. Across the region, only Stratford-on-Avon, with 28.4%, had a lower percentage.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in Malvern Hills increased by 2.4 percentage points

Change in employment

Of Malvern Hills residents aged 16 years and over, 52.4% said they were employed (excluding full-time students) in 2021, down from 54.3% in 2011.

In 2021, just over 1 in 50 people (2.1%) said they were unemployed, compared with 2.7% in 2011. The percentage of retired Malvern Hills residents increased from 29.3% to 31.3%.

The decrease in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were employed was greater in Malvern Hills (1.9 percentage points) than across the West Midlands (1.1 percentage points, from 54.4% to 53.3%). Across England, the percentage fell by 0.8 percentage points, from 56.5% to 55.7%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were employed (excluding full-time students) in Malvern Hills decreased by 1.9 percentage points

Ethnic groups in Malvern Hills

In 2021, 1.4% of Malvern Hills residents identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category, up from 0.9% in 2011. The 0.6 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across the West Midlands, the percentage of people from "Mixed or Multiple ethnic groups" increased from 2.4% to 3.0%, while across England the percentage increased from 2.3% to 3.0%.

In 2021, 96.6% of people in Malvern Hills identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 97.6% in 2011), while 1.3% identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category (compared with 1.2% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Other" category ("Arab" or "Any other ethnic group") increased from 0.1% in 2011 to 0.3% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.
